review_type: GitHub branch-wide scoped source and defensive-controls review

findings.title: Individual web skill exporter accepts an unverified declared source SHA
findings.observation: export_skill validates source_sha only against 40-char hex syntax; reads working files and produces a deterministic ZIP without verifying Git HEAD, source tree or Git blob identity. Tests use an arbitrary mock SHA.
findings.impact: A package may falsely claim provenance from a different source SHA; not a verified observed exploit.
findings.recommended_action: Pin Git HEAD and clean tree, bind packaged contents to tracked Git blobs and manifest; test wrong SHA/modified files/symlinks.

findings.title: Unhashable receipt entry may crash evaluation validation
findings.observation: validate_trial calls set(verified_tool_receipts) before checking each receipt element is a string; a nested list/dict can raise TypeError instead of yielding a reasoned denial.
findings.impact: Untrusted malformed trial records can interrupt a batch evaluation; this reference code is not shipped in skills-only runtime.
findings.recommended_action: Check receipt type/nonblank before uniqueness; catch malformed input fail-closed; execute regression negatives.

findings.title: Cross-case evaluation receipt replay not rejected at report aggregation
findings.observation: A duplicate receipt inside a single case is rejected, but report only rejects duplicate case/arm pairs and does not enforce uniqueness of receipt across different cases/arms.
findings.impact: A poorly implemented proof adapter could double-credit reused source receipts in provisional scores; external proof adapter is currently absent.
findings.recommended_action: Require global receipt uniqueness and source/case/action binding, with negative tests. Preserve provisional not release-accepted classification.

findings.title: Owner-managed runner source execution has conditional unsafe-write exposure
findings.observation: Workflow executes checked-out source tests on persistent self-hosted runners for integration pushes. SHA checks, pinned checkout and read-only token mitigate, but write protections and actor permissions require fresh live verification.
findings.impact: Unapproved writer could cause code to run on owner development machines if branch write controls are insufficient; no compromise observed.
findings.recommended_action: Inspect active branch rules, permissions and runner isolation; require reviewed source prior to runner execution; do not modify permissions or trigger runner without authorization.

findings.title: V0.0.2 real browser host acceptance absent
findings.observation: Eleven H-01–H-11 actual host trials remain NOT_RUN and canonical private plugin inspected at v0.0.1.
findings.impact: Reference code passes do not establish installed plugin or supported browser-host behavior.
findings.recommended_action: Execute permissioned real-host acceptance only with appropriate owner approval; do not release meantime.

findings.title: Independent specialist quality measurements absent
findings.observation: 270 authored synthetic cases, 54 visible unblinded reservations, zero independent oracle approvals and zero actual model-host trial evidence at baseline; 270 reference router tests are not 270 model trials.
findings.impact: Cannot make evidence-backed claims of specialist precision, recall or incident handling quality.
findings.recommended_action: Secure independent oracle/scoring protocol and real permitted host evidence; preserve NOT_MEASURED until validated.

findings.title: Synthetic Blue alert sample lacks event identifiers needed by its own acceptance text
findings.observation: blue-team:normal:01 has aggregated denial counts but no enumerated event IDs, while its model-authored proposed oracle asks to cite source event IDs.
findings.impact: An evaluator may wrongly reward fabricated event identifiers or penalize appropriate source-gap reporting.
findings.recommended_action: Supply dated, identifiable synthetic events or make absence of event IDs the explicit expected finding.

warning: This register records source review, risks, and release gates; none is a confirmed production intrusion or independently certified exploit.
